facts.text: The README states that the SDK connects to one or two data gloves over a serial port at 1 Mbps and samples at 120 Hz
The README lists 19 tensile sensors
The README documents tensile_data as 19 integers in the range 0-16384 and marks acc_data, gyro_data and mag_data as 'To be added'
The user guide lists 19 sensors, a 120 Hz frequency and a sensor value range of 0 - 16380
The SDK constant SENSOR_MAX_VALUE is 8192 * 2
The reader skips a packet whose tensile values are not all within 0..SENSOR_MAX_VALUE
The SDK's DEFAULT_BAUDRATE is 1000000
GloveSensorData documents the packet units: accelerometer in m/s2, gyroscope in rad/s, magnetometer in uT, temperature in Celsius and timestamp in microseconds
The packet is 132 bytes: 19 int32 tensile values, three float accelerometer values, three float gyroscope values, three float magnetometer values, one float temperature and one uint32 timestamp
parse_raw_data unpacks exactly those fields from the packet offsets
The reader validates a packet with a CRC-32 over the first 120 bytes
get_raw_data waits, with no timeout, until the queue has a packet and returns only the most recent one after draining the queue
get_data reads the most recent raw packet and parses it
OpenCyberGlove refuses construction unless at least one of left_port and right_port is provided
start connects each configured glove and starts its background reader
stop stops the readers of all configured gloves
get_data(hand_type) returns the packet of the requested glove and raises RuntimeError when that glove is not configured
stop_reader clears the reader event and joins the reader thread without a timeout
stop_reader does not close the serial port and does not clear the data queue, so packets already queued remain after a stop
connect opens the serial port with a one-second read timeout
calibrate prints a pose prompt and waits on input() before its min/max samples, then prompts again for the static-average samples
advanced_calibrate collects each pose through data_collection, which also waits on input()
inference raises NotImplementedError for method='linear'; method='model' requires an ONNX model
The safety guide states that the glove is an input-only device and does not provide haptic feedback or collision protection
The safety guide states that an integrator controlling robots or mechanical arms is responsible for collision detection, limit switches and emergency stops in the controlled system
The safety guide asks for a safety officer and immediate access to the emergency stop button when operating physical equipment
